content: Upstream stimulatory factor 1 (USF1) is a protein encoded by the USF1 gene in humans. This gene belongs to the basic helix-loop-helix leucine zipper (bHLH-LZ) family and plays a role as a cellular transcription factor. The USF1 protein is capable of activating transcription by binding to pyrimidine-rich initiator (Inr) elements and E-box motifs within target gene promoters. The USF1 gene has been associated with familial combined hyperlipidemia (FCHL), a genetic disorder characterized by elevated levels of cholesterol and triglycerides, which increases the risk of cardiovascular disease. Two distinct transcript variants of the USF1 gene have been identified, each encoding different isoforms of the protein. Research conducted in mice has indicated that reduced levels of USF1 may enhance metabolic activity in brown adipose tissue, suggesting a potential role in energy homeostasis and thermogenesis. USF1 has been shown to interact with several other proteins, including USF2 (another member of the same transcription factor family), FOSL1 (a component of the AP-1 transcription factor complex), and GTF2I (general transcription factor II-I), highlighting its involvement in complex regulatory networks that control gene expression.
